issues.legal_issue: An ongoing obstruction of a public street constitutes a continuing wrong for limitation purposes.
material_facts: The suit sought removal of an encroachment that obstructed use of a public street.
The encroachment and resulting obstruction continued when the suit was filed.
A prior proceeding had directed the parties to resolve disputed facts through a civil suit, which was filed thereafter.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by limitation because the continuing obstruction gave rise to a continuing cause of action.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22 of the Limitation Act, 1963 provides that a fresh limitation period begins at every moment during which a continuing tort persists. Section 3 requires a court to consider limitation even if the issue was not raised earlier. Relying on Sankar Dastidar v. Shrimati Banjula Dastidar and Anr., AIR 2007 SC 514, the Court applied the principle that continuing interference with a right of way gives rise to continuing breaches.

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_removal_of_public_obstr: A person brought a civil suit seeking removal of an obstruction to a public way.
predicates.obstruction_continues: The obstruction and resulting interference with use of the public way persisted when the suit was brought.

issues.definition: When a civil suit seeks removal of a public obstruction that persists, the suit is not barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose own use of community property is affected may sue to remove an encroachment without satisfying the requirements for a representative suit.
material_facts: The plaintiff alleged that the disputed street was for common use and that the encroachment prejudicially affected his own right to use it.
Although the suit was presented in a representative capacity, the plaintiff was personally affected by the alleged encroachment.
issues.conclusion: The suit was maintainable notwithstanding the alleged non-compliance with the requirements for a representative suit.
issues.legal_principle: Order I Rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires court permission for a suit brought representatively. Relying on Kalyan Singh, London Trained Cutter, Johri Bazar, Jaipur v. Smt. Chhoti and Ors., AIR 1990 SC 396, the Court held that a person may sue individually to assert a right in community property or seek removal of an encroachment affecting that person, without complying with Order I Rule 8.

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_removal_of_community_pr: A person brought a civil suit seeking removal of an encroachment from property used in common by a community.
predicates.plaintiff_personally_affected: The plaintiff's own right to use the community property was prejudicially affected by the encroachment.

issues.definition: A person personally affected by an encroachment on community property may maintain an individual suit to remove it.

issues.legal_issue: Evidence establishing the existence of a public street and an encroachment on it can support a finding of encroachment despite the absence of the official evidence alleged to be necessary.
material_facts: A public officer testified and proved a report that identified encroachment on the disputed street.
The person who had laid out the colony testified that a street had been left beside the plots, and the site plan and sale-deed evidence showed the street.
Other witnesses corroborated an admission by a co-defendant that he had encroached on the street and later removed that encroachment.
The appellant's evidence consisted of his denial that the disputed property was part of the street.
All three courts found that the disputed land was part of the public street and that the appellant had encroached on it.
issues.conclusion: The evidence supported the findings that the land was part of a public street and that the appellant had encroached on it; the Court found no infirmity in the concurrent judgments.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the evidence as a whole, including testimony, a proved official report, the site plan, and sale-deed evidence, and treated the lower courts' conclusions as concurrent findings of fact. It found no rule requiring the appellant's challenge to succeed merely because the particular official document or witness he said was necessary had not been produced.

predicates.appeal_challenges_concurrent_encroachmen: A party appealed against concurrent lower-court findings that land was a public way and had been encroached upon.
predicates.evidence_supports_public_way: Testimony or documentary evidence supported the finding that the disputed land formed part of a public way.
predicates.evidence_supports_encroachment: Evidence supported the finding that the appellant had encroached on the public way.

issues.definition: On an appeal challenging concurrent findings of encroachment, those findings are upheld when evidence supports both the public-way finding and the encroachment finding.
